READING PASSAGE 2

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 14–26, which are based on Reading Passage 2 below.

The internal body clock

Each of our cells has an internal 'clock' which dictates our daily rhythms. But why?

A From buffalo to bacteria, oaks to algae, all life follows the same relentless 24-hour cycle, which is driven by the rising and setting of the Sun. Or is it? Over 250 years ago, a French scientist performed a simple experiment that blew apart the idea that all life on Earth does the bidding of the Sun. Intrigued by the way some flowers open and close their leaves each day, Jean-Jacques de Mairan put a heliotrope in a darkened room and observed the effect. He was expecting the plant, robbed of sunlight, to cease its daily routine. To his astonishment, its leaves continued to open and close as if in response to some invisible timekeeper.

B But what – and where – is this internal timekeeper? And how does it achieve such astonishing regularity? These are the mysteries at the forefront of chronobiology, the study of the effect of time in living organisms. The search for answers is about more than just tying up some scientific loose ends. Internal ‘clocks’ clearly cause a lot of hardship. When an individual’s ‘clock’ is knocked out of synchronization through having to work at night or go on long-haul flights, that person can be left utterly unable to think or act. Yet even when these ‘clocks’ work correctly, the natural rhythms of alertness they generate prove dangerous: traffic accident statistics show two deadly peaks, at 4 a.m. and again twelve hours later when people are at their least alert.

C During the 1970s, best-selling books began to emerge claiming such phenomena were manifestations of so-called biorhythms, a set of three cycles governing physical, emotional and intellectual traits. Said to start from the moment of birth and repeat every 23, 28 and 33 days respectively, they were supposed to result in ‘critical days’ when one or more cycles led to sub-optimal performance, with unfortunate consequences.

D Scientists have since dismissed biorhythms as pseudoscience, insisting the existence of the three cycles has no basis in fact. In 1998, Dr Terence Hines of Pace University, New York State published the most comprehensive study of the claims made for biorhythms, reviewing the results of over 130 investigations. He found that three-quarters of them failed to provide any support for biorhythms. Most of the remainder contained blunders ranging from faulty mathematics to basic errors in statistics, while the handful of positive studies were explicable as flukes.

E But there is no doubting the existence of 24-hour biological cycles – or, rather, ones roughly 24 hours long. Following de Mairan’s pioneering work, other researchers found that when deprived of the cues provided by sunlight, organisms settle down to ‘free-running’ cycles that are close to, but rarely exactly, 24 hours long. In the case of humans, the cycle is typically around 24.5 hours long. This is the so-called ‘circadian’ cycle (from the Latin meaning ‘about a day’), the length of which is generated by the mysterious internal ‘clock’.

F During the late 1960s, chronobiologists believed they had found the ‘clock’, in the form of the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN), a collection of nerves in a region of the brain known as the hypothalamus. Linked to photosensitive cells in the eye, the SCN senses daylight and triggers the release of hormones like melatonin, which keep body functions in synchronization with the time of day. For a few years the SCN was regarded as the ultimate pacemaker – at least in higher organisms such as ourselves. But in 1971, scientists at the California Institute of Technology working with fruit flies found evidence for something truly amazing. Fruit flies appeared to have genes affecting the daily rhythm of their behavior – suggesting that there are ‘clocks’ inside each of their cells. Further evidence for this emerged in 1995, when researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital isolated nerve cells from the SCN, and found they kept up a circadian cycle without help from daylight. Finally in 1997, scientists at Northwestern University, Illinois, found a gene that regulates the daily rhythms of cellular activity in mammals.

G The details of how this gene, known as CLOCK, actually works are still being investigated, but they could culminate in better ways of coping with shift-work and jet-lag. Professor Takahashi, who led the research, says that now that we know that circadian clocks exist throughout our bodies, we will need new strategies and therapeutics to reset all of our cells. But how do all the biochemical ‘clocks’ inside their cells stay in synchronization and why did organisms bother to acquire a link with sunlight? So far, no-one knows, though there are several theories. For example, sunlight might be useful in keeping the myriad cellular ‘clocks’ in lockstep.

H In the search for answers, researchers are studying the behavior of a microbe called cyanobacterium. In 2005, a team at Nagoya University, Japan, showed that chemical reactions between three proteins produced by this bacterium ebbed and flowed on a 24-hour cycle. Cyanobacterium is the oldest form of life on Earth, so this suggests that cellular ‘clocks’ have existed for over three billion years. All subsequent organisms have followed suit, says Professor Johnson of Vanderbilt University, Tennessee. ‘Bacteria, fungi, plants and animals all appear to have evolved clock systems independently from each other.’ Quite why is still unknown. But one thing is clear: the daily routine of life is certainly not a modern invention.

questionGroups.bodyHtml:
Questions 14–18

Reading Passage 2 has eight paragraphs, A–H.

Which paragraph contains the following information?

Write the correct letter, A–H, in boxes 14–18 on your answer sheet.

ABCDEFGH
14 support for an earlier finding from experiments on insects
15 criticism of the way some research data was analysed
16 reference to a basic test on a plant
17a statement that the length of natural cycles varies slightly between living things
18 reference to a theory that became popular with the public

Questions 19–22

Complete the summary below.

Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage for each answer.

Write your answers in boxes 19–22 on your answer sheet.

An overview of research into the existence of the internal ‘clock’

Towards the end of the 1960s, research into the SCN, which is located in the hypothalamus, led chronobiologists to believe they had found the internal ‘clock’ at last. Their theory was based on the fact that certain hormones that regulate the timing of physical functions are controlled by the SCN. The SCN is able to perceive 19 as a result of connections to the eye.

Several years later, research involving 20 showed that the timing of their normal actions was regulated by certain 21 , or ‘clocks’, in their cells. Thus the internal ‘clock’ is not an individual mechanism, as previously thought, but exists within each cell. Other scientists went on to conduct experiments in the dark that proved that a 22 was maintained by individual SCN cells.

Questions 23 and 24

Choose TWO letters, A–E.

Write the correct letters in boxes 23 and 24 on your answer sheet.

Which TWO of the following problems are stated as being linked with the internal ‘clock’?

Questions 25 and 26

Choose TWO letters, A–E.

Write the correct letters in boxes 25 and 26 on your answer sheet.

Which TWO of the following issues relating to internal ‘clocks’ remain to be solved, according to information in the passage?

items.text:
（1）题目 14：support for an earlier finding from experiments on insects
题目翻译：为早先通过昆虫实验得出的发现提供支持。
答案：F
定位：正文 F 段，后半部
原文：Further evidence for this emerged in 1995, when researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital isolated nerve cells from the SCN, and found they kept up a circadian cycle without help from daylight.
译文：1995年又出现了进一步证据：研究者分离出SCN神经细胞，发现它们无需日光帮助仍能维持昼夜周期。

解析：Further evidence 对应 support，this 指向前文果蝇实验显示细胞内部存在“时钟”的发现，所以选 F。

（2）题目 15：criticism of the way some research data was analysed
题目翻译：批评某些研究数据的分析方式。
答案：D
定位：正文 D 段，第3句
原文：Most of the remainder contained blunders ranging from faulty mathematics to basic errors in statistics
译文：其余大多数研究包含从数学计算错误到基础统计错误等问题。

解析：faulty mathematics 和 errors in statistics 都是数据分析方法上的错误，因此选 D。

（3）题目 16：reference to a basic test on a plant
题目翻译：提到对植物进行的一项简单测试。
答案：A
定位：正文 A 段，中部
原文：Jean-Jacques de Mairan put a heliotrope in a darkened room and observed the effect.
译文：Jean-Jacques de Mairan 把一株天芥菜放进黑暗房间并观察结果。

解析：把植物放入暗室观察叶片开合，是题干所说的 basic test on a plant，因此选 A。

（4）题目 17：a statement that the length of natural cycles varies slightly between living things
题目翻译：说明不同生物的自然周期长度会略有差异。
答案：E
定位：正文 E 段，第2至3句
原文：organisms settle down to ‘free-running’ cycles that are close to, but rarely exactly, 24 hours long. In the case of humans, the cycle is typically around 24.5 hours long.
译文：生物的自由运行周期接近但很少恰好为24小时；人类通常约为24.5小时。

解析：rarely exactly 24 hours 与人类约24.5小时的例子说明不同生物周期存在轻微差异，所以选 E。

（5）题目 18：reference to a theory that became popular with the public
题目翻译：提到一种曾在公众中流行的理论。
答案：C
定位：正文 C 段，第1句
原文：During the 1970s, best-selling books began to emerge claiming such phenomena were manifestations of so-called biorhythms
译文：20世纪70年代，宣称这些现象是所谓“生物节律”表现的畅销书开始出现。

解析：best-selling books 表明该理论受到公众欢迎，理论名称是 biorhythms，所以选 C。

（1）题目 19：Towards the end of the 1960s, research into the SCN, which is located in the hypothalamus, led chronobiologists to believe they had found the internal ‘clock’ at last. Their theory was based on the fact that certain hormones that regulate the timing of physical functions are controlled by the SCN. The SCN is able to perceive ________ as a result of connections to the eye.
题目翻译：SCN 与眼睛相连，因此能够感知________。
答案：daylight
定位：正文 F 段，第2句
原文：Linked to photosensitive cells in the eye, the SCN senses daylight
译文：SCN 与眼睛中的感光细胞相连，能够感知日光。

解析：perceive 对应 senses，connections to the eye 对应 linked to photosensitive cells in the eye，因此填 daylight。

（2）题目 20：Several years later, research involving ________ showed that the timing of their normal actions was regulated by certain ________, or ‘clocks’, in their cells. Thus the internal ‘clock’ is not an individual mechanism, as previously thought, but exists within each cell. Other scientists went on to conduct experiments in the dark that proved that a ________ was maintained by individual SCN cells.
题目翻译：之后以________为对象的研究显示，它们日常行为的节奏由细胞内的某些机制调节。
答案：fruit flies
定位：正文 F 段，第4句
原文：scientists at the California Institute of Technology working with fruit flies found evidence for something truly amazing.
译文：加州理工学院的科学家通过研究果蝇发现了令人惊讶的证据。

解析：research involving 对应 working with，实验对象是 fruit flies；两词且均为原文连续词组。

（3）题目 21：Several years later, research involving ________ showed that the timing of their normal actions was regulated by certain ________, or ‘clocks’, in their cells. Thus the internal ‘clock’ is not an individual mechanism, as previously thought, but exists within each cell. Other scientists went on to conduct experiments in the dark that proved that a ________ was maintained by individual SCN cells.
题目翻译：果蝇日常行为的节奏由细胞内的某些________，也就是“时钟”，来调节。
答案：genes
定位：正文 F 段，第5句
原文：Fruit flies appeared to have genes affecting the daily rhythm of their behavior – suggesting that there are ‘clocks’ inside each of their cells.
译文：果蝇似乎拥有影响日常行为节律的基因，这表明每个细胞内都存在“时钟”。

解析：题干 regulated by 对应 affecting，or clocks 对应原文将这些 genes 与细胞内“时钟”联系起来，因此填 genes。

（4）题目 22：Several years later, research involving ________ showed that the timing of their normal actions was regulated by certain ________, or ‘clocks’, in their cells. Thus the internal ‘clock’ is not an individual mechanism, as previously thought, but exists within each cell. Other scientists went on to conduct experiments in the dark that proved that a ________ was maintained by individual SCN cells.
题目翻译：黑暗实验表明，单个SCN细胞仍能维持一个________。
答案：circadian cycle
定位：正文 F 段，第6句
原文：isolated nerve cells from the SCN, and found they kept up a circadian cycle without help from daylight.
译文：研究者分离出SCN神经细胞，发现它们无需日光帮助仍能维持昼夜周期。

解析：maintained 对应 kept up，individual SCN cells 对应 isolated nerve cells from the SCN，因此填连续原文词组 circadian cycle。

（1）题目 25：（题干见题目区）
题目翻译：根据文章，下列哪两个有关内部时钟的问题仍未解决？
答案：C（the reason for living beings forming a connection with the Sun’s rhythms）
定位：正文 G 段，第3至4句
原文：why did organisms bother to acquire a link with sunlight? So far, no-one knows
译文：生物为什么要形成与阳光的联系？到目前为止，没有人知道。

解析：organisms 对应 living beings，a link with sunlight 对应 a connection with the Sun’s rhythms；So far, no-one knows 明确说明原因仍未解决，所以选 C。

（2）题目 26：（题干见题目区）
题目翻译：根据文章，下列哪两个有关内部时钟的问题仍未解决？
答案：D（the way in which all ‘clocks’ in a single organism are able to stay in step with one another）
定位：正文 G 段，第3至4句
原文：But how do all the biochemical ‘clocks’ inside their cells stay in synchronization and why did organisms bother to acquire a link with sunlight? So far, no-one knows
译文：但是，细胞内部的所有生化“时钟”如何保持同步？生物又为什么要形成与阳光的联系？到目前为止，没有人知道。

解析：all the biochemical ‘clocks’ inside their cells 对应 all ‘clocks’ in a single organism，stay in synchronization 对应 stay in step with one another；no-one knows 表明该机制仍未解决，所以选 D。
